I went through all 80 rules in the checklist against `git diff f4937ec08…HEAD` (17 files, all under `apps/web` and `packages/utils`). Five rules fail. Nothing was modified: the checklist went to the scratchpad, and I didn't run tests or `gh`.

## Findings

**1. DATA-05: an address compared without `sameAddress`** (confirmed)
`apps/web/src/components/nested-safes/NestedSafesList/useManageNestedSafes.ts:177`
The new `getSimilarAddresses` filter uses `a.toLowerCase() !== address.toLowerCase()`. The rule asks for `sameAddress(a, b)` on any address equality check. The same PR also removed the `sameAddress` import from `useOnboardingSafes.ts`. Its replacement there is a set lookup on lowercased values (`trustedAddresses.has(address.toLowerCase())`), which is fine; this line in `useManageNestedSafes.ts` is the only true violation.

**2. PROD-01: the always-on look-alike rule got broader with no stated product decision** (confirmed)
`packages/utils/src/utils/addressSimilarity.ts:133`, used through `apps/web/src/features/address-poisoning/hooks/useSimilarityClusters.ts:25`
- **Before:** addresses were flagged only when they shared the front **and** the back characters (the old prefix+suffix bucket in `detectSimilarAddresses`).
- **After:** web lists use `detectListClusters`, which flags addresses that share the front-4 **or** the back-4, and chains matches together.
- The comments say this part is "always on", so it is not behind `ADDRESS_POISONING_PROTECTION`.
- **User impact:** users will see many more badges, confirm prompts, and Select-all exclusions on five surfaces: onboarding, add-accounts, space safe-accounts, the trusted-safes modal and nested safes. That happens even with the flag off.
- **Mobile mismatch:** mobile still uses the old rule (`apps/mobile/src/features/Send/hooks/useSuspiciousAddressDetection.ts`), so the two platforms now disagree.

Either cite the product/design decision in the PR, or put the OR rule behind the flag.

**3. PROD-01 / DATA-01: a Safe trusted on one chain now counts as trusted on every chain** (confirmed)
`apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/SelectSafesOnboarding/hooks/useOnboardingSafes.ts:41-66`
Trust used to be decided per chain and address. Now an address pinned on any one chain moves all of its owned or undeployed chain copies into "trusted" and out of "owned". Because the flagged set is filtered to owned Safes only (`:79`), those copies also stop getting look-alike warnings in onboarding. The change looks deliberate, going by the comment, but it is visible behaviour outside the stated scope (address-poisoning clustering) and needs explicit product sign-off.

**4. TEST-02: the new cross-chain trusted branch has no test** (confirmed)
`apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/SelectSafesOnboarding/hooks/useOnboardingSafes.ts:46`
The existing `__tests__/useOnboardingSafes.test.ts` covers "excludes trusted safes from owned list" and multi-chain grouping only for owned Safes. No case pins a Safe on chain 1, has it owned on chain 137, and checks that both copies land under trusted and none under owned.

**5. TEST-02 / TEST-04: changed logic in the similarity hooks has no tests** (confirmed)
- `apps/web/src/components/nested-safes/NestedSafesList/useManageNestedSafes.ts:172`: `getSimilarAddresses` was rewritten to rebuild groups from `groupIdByAddress` plus the address list. `groupSafesBySimilarity` and the flagged gate on `selectAll` switched source. This hook has no test file.
- `apps/web/src/features/address-poisoning/hooks/useSimilarityClusters.ts:21`: this new hook has no test of its own. Its "anchor-only match is flagged but has no group id" branch goes untested. The imitated-original branch is only covered indirectly, through `useFlaggedSimilarAddresses.test.ts`.

## Minor (not tied to a rule)

- **Comment density:** `AGENTS.md` says "Treat code comments as tech debt". The diff adds long explanatory comments at nearly every call site, e.g. `ManageTrustedSafesContent.tsx:100-101`, `useTrustedSafesModal.ts:110-112` and `useManageNestedSafes.ts:71-73`. The same "Intra-list … + anchor … (flag-gated)" note is repeated in 5 files. The JSDoc on the hooks already carries it.
- **Duplicated helper:** the `isAddressFlagged = useCallback(a => flaggedAll.has(a.toLowerCase()))` wrapper is written twice (`useTrustedSafesModal.ts:114`, `useManageNestedSafes.ts:75`). `useSimilarityClusters` could return it once.
- **Stale doc (API-01-adjacent):** `apps/web/docs/spaces-accounts-architecture.md:231-236` still shows `detectSimilarAddresses` for space similarity. This PR moves web off it, so the doc is now further out of date. `getFlaggedSimilarAddressSet` has no callers left outside its own module and tests.
- **Misleading test name:** `useFlaggedSimilarAddresses.test.ts:34` calls its case "the flag-off path", but it only returns an empty anchor map and never turns the feature flag off.

## Rules that passed

- **FEAT-01 / FEAT-02 / FEAT-03:** cross-feature imports go through the `@/features/address-poisoning` barrel, hooks are exported directly as `apps/web/AGENTS.md` requires, and nothing inside the feature imports its own barrel.
- **TEST-01 / TEST-05:** the new assertions would catch the regressions they claim to cover, and no test imports MSW fixtures.
- **DATA-06:** normalization matches between the anchor keys and the list keys.
- **Memoization:** every caller passes a stable, memoized `addresses` array.
- The remaining rules (auth, mobile, CI, transactions, RTK and so on) don't apply to this diff.

I read the linked example for FEAT-01 and FEAT-02 in `apps/web/AGENTS.md`. I didn't use any Level 1 or Level 2 zoom (review-learning lookups).
